meta.title: Mikania micrantha comparative-genomic priors on VNIR reflectance

findings.claim: Sixteen positively-selected genes concentrated in photoreaction and the utilisation of photoassimilates
findings.source: Liu B. et al. (2020) Nature Communications 11:340
findings.note: Selection scan on the chromosome-scale assembly. Positive selection acting on photoreaction genes implies the light reactions themselves, not just growth rate, are the target of adaptation — which is what makes a *pigment* and *photosystem* difference plausible rather than a generic vigour difference.

findings.claim: Enhanced photosynthetic capacity via night-time CO2 absorption supplementing daytime carbon fixation
findings.source: Liu B. et al. (2020) Nature Communications 11:340
findings.note: A CAM-like supplementary carbon route in an otherwise C3 vine. Relevant here mainly because it implies elevated whole-plant carbon gain and therefore supports the high-SLA / fast-turnover leaf economics inference (T3), and because it predicts a DIURNAL component to any spectral difference — which is an acquisition-window constraint, not just a band choice.

findings.claim: Elevated stem photosynthesis efficiency — photosynthetically active tissue outside the leaf lamina
findings.source: Liu B. et al. (2020) Nature Communications 11:340
findings.note: The single most operationally useful finding in the whole literature for this product. A green stem is a chlorophyll-bearing surface with a very different internal structure from a leaf: little spongy mesophyll, so it scatters far less in the NIR while still absorbing in the red. A canopy blanket that mixes leaf and photosynthetic stem therefore has a *shallower NIR plateau relative to its red absorption depth* than a pure-leaf canopy of the same greenness. That is a shape difference, not an amplitude difference, and shape survives illumination variation (proposal §3.2, NIR row).

findings.claim: ~half the genome is LTR retrotransposon, 80% from an expansion within the last ~1 Myr, plus a whole-genome duplication and recent segmental duplications
findings.source: Liu B. et al. (2020) Nature Communications 11:340; Wang et al. (2025) New Phytologist
findings.note: Genome architecture, not phenotype. Included because it is the mechanism by which gene-family dosage changes (F5) arose, and because it is the part of the story that is unambiguously established — useful for credibility even though it makes no direct spectral prediction. Deliberately given no spectral prediction below; a desk study that turns every genomic fact into a band prediction is not a desk study, it is astrology.

findings.claim: Gene family expansion and transposable-element dynamics associated with invasiveness; population structure resolved
findings.source: Wang et al. (2025) New Phytologist — chromosome-scale M. micrantha (~1.53 Gb) and native congener M. cordata (~1.68 Gb)
findings.note: Supplies the direct comparative contrast against a *native congener*, which is the closest published analogue of the discrimination problem AFCD has. Population structure is the hook for the §3.4 roadmap item (regrowth vs recolonisation at treated sites).

findings.claim: Evolution and diurnal expression patterns of photosynthetic pathway genes diverge from congeners
findings.source: The Crop Journal (2023) — diurnal expression of photosynthetic pathway genes in M. micrantha
findings.note: Diurnal divergence is the reason this project constrains its acquisition window rather than flying whenever the weather allows. If the transcriptional difference has a time-of-day structure, the phenotype plausibly does too, and an inconsistent solar window would add a nuisance factor that looks exactly like species variance.

findings.claim: Comparative transcriptomics against native congeners shows divergence in photosynthesis and secondary-metabolite pathways
findings.source: Comparative transcriptome analysis of M. micrantha with native congeners
findings.note: Independent replication of the light-and-carbon convergence in F1/F2/F3 by a different method on different material. Two methods agreeing is the reason §4.2 can call the science "published, replicated in adjacent species, and consistent" rather than a single-paper result.

findings.claim: Defensive secondary-metabolite mechanisms likely enhance invasiveness
findings.source: Defensive Mechanisms of Mikania micrantha ... (2025)
findings.note: The basis for the anthocyanin / flavonoid row of the §3.2 table. Weakest link in the set: "secondary metabolite pathway divergence" is a long way from "a measurable 550-580 nm shoulder", and the desk study scores it accordingly rather than flattering it.

traits.trait: Altered standing chlorophyll pool and chlorophyll a/b ratio
traits.rationale: Selection on photoreaction genes and divergent expression of photosynthetic pathway genes act on the light-harvesting apparatus. Light-harvesting complex composition sets the chlorophyll a/b ratio and the total pigment pool per unit leaf area. This is the least contentious of the trait inferences, but it is still an inference: transcript abundance is not pigment concentration.

traits.trait: Chlorophyll-bearing, low-mesophyll stem tissue contributing to the canopy signal
traits.rationale: Directly implied by the published finding rather than inferred at a distance — elevated stem photosynthesis requires chlorophyll in the stem. The inference is only about the *proportion of a canopy patch* that this tissue occupies at 8 cm GSD, which is a canopy-architecture question the ground library must measure.

traits.trait: High specific leaf area, thin lamina, rapid leaf turnover
traits.rationale: The classic fast-growth end of the leaf economics spectrum, consistent with a vine that blankets a canopy in a season. Thin lamina means fewer internal air-cell interfaces and therefore a lower NIR plateau — but this is an AMPLITUDE effect, and §3.2 warns that amplitude differences are confounded by illumination. Ranked accordingly.

traits.trait: Divergent flavonoid / anthocyanin standing pools
traits.rationale: Weak chain, honestly labelled. Defensive-chemistry divergence need not touch the specific pigments that absorb in the visible, and anthocyanin is the most environmentally labile pigment of the three (config/default.yaml `nuisance` gives it the largest within-class CV for that reason).

traits.trait: Two-layer blanket: vine layer draped over, not integrated into, host canopy
traits.rationale: Growth-habit trait rather than a molecular one; the genomic findings support only the growth *rate* that makes the habit possible. Included because the resulting mixed-pixel structure is what makes unmixing the right tool (§3.2, final paragraph), and because that is a structural prediction the imagery can test independently of any pigment claim.

ranked_operational.measures: Wavelength of maximum first derivative across the red edge
ranked_operational.falsification: Mikania mean REP does not exceed the native-climber mean REP by at least 1 nm in the ground spectral library, in either season, at p < 0.05 by a site-blocked test.
ranked_operational.why_broadband_misses: Multispectral gives a red-edge BAND, not a POSITION.

acquisition_constraints.constraint: Restrict acquisition to a fixed solar-time window; do not mix morning and afternoon sorties within a comparison
acquisition_constraints.rationale: Night-time CO2 uptake and diurnally-structured expression of photosynthetic genes both imply the physiological state — and therefore plausibly the pigment and water status driving P1, P5 and P8 — varies through the day. A time-of-day difference between two flights would masquerade as a species or site difference. This is a batch effect in the §5.1(7) sense, and the control is design, not correction.
acquisition_constraints.cost_consequence: Narrows usable hours below the ~8 h daylight assumption in §5.2, worsening §5.3 coverage economics

acquisition_constraints.constraint: A constitutive photosystem signal should be measured OUT of the flowering window to be worth anything
acquisition_constraints.rationale: §6.1(2) claims year-round capability on the grounds that a constitutive photosystem signal is more temporally stable than a transient flowering one. That claim is only tested by measuring in the foliage-only season. Measuring in bloom and inferring the rest would be assuming the conclusion.
acquisition_constraints.cost_consequence: Requires at least two acquisition seasons in Phase 0 — already budgeted in §7.3 item 1

headline: 8 falsifiable spectral predictions derived from 8 published genomic, transcriptomic and physiological findings via 5 inferred trait chains. Every chain terminates in an `inferred_optical` step: no leaf-optical measurement linking these genes to reflectance exists for Hong Kong material. These are the measurements the Phase 0 spectroradiometer campaign should make, ranked by what is worth measuring rather than by what is best cited.
